name: Nationalparkhaus Matrei
kurzbeschreibung: The Nationalparkhaus Matrei offers interactive insights into the impressive wildlife and flora of the Nationalpark Hohe Tauern.
preis: Erwachsene ca. 8 €, Kinder ca. 4 € (mit Osttirol Card kostenlos)
beschreibung:
Overview

The Nationalparkhaus Matrei stands as the architectural and interpretive gateway to Hohe Tauern National Park in East Tyrol. Situated in the center of Matrei in Osttirol, this cutting-edge visitor and educational pavilion invites nature enthusiasts of all ages on an inspiring journey across Central Europe's largest wilderness reserve. The exhibition centerpiece is the interactive permanent gallery "Tauernblicke – Moments of Wonder": across two light-filled floors, multimedia terminals, lifelike alpine wildlife displays, and 3D topographic relief models illuminate the harsh ecological zones spanning between the ice-crowned summits of the Großglockner (3,798 m) and Großvenediger (3,657 m). The primary draw is the immersive 360-degree panoramic cinema, which projects visitors directly into cascading glacier torrents, thundering avalanches, and the silent thermals of golden eagles and alpine ibex. The visitor center also serves as the operational headquarters coordinating educational backcountry treks led by certified national park rangers.

Route & Requirements

The Nationalparkhaus Matrei is designed as an all-weather, universally accessible experience ideal for families, student groups, seniors, and nature lovers. All exhibition galleries, multimedia consoles, and the panoramic theatre are barrier-free and serviced by elevators (easy grade T1, fully wheelchair and stroller accessible). Visitors typically spend between 1.5 and 2.5 hours absorbing the exhibits and documentary screenings. Youngsters enjoy hands-on ranger discovery stations featuring touchable stone minerals and interactive animal track puzzles. The center acts as the departure hub for official ranger-led expeditions, ranging from gentle meadow strolls to high-altitude glacier excursions into neighboring valleys such as Gschlößtal, Virgental, and Kals. A dedicated national park boutique stocks artisanal Tyrolean crafts and topographical trail maps. For hygiene reasons, pet dogs are not allowed within exhibition halls, though shaded outdoor waiting zones are provided.

Visit & Arrival

Rail travelers arrive via ÖBB trains into Lienz station and connect to regional Postbus line 951, departing regularly toward Matrei in Osttirol (stopping at "Matrei i. O. Mittelschule / Nationalparkhaus" immediately beside the entrance). Drivers reach Matrei via the scenic Felbertauern highway B108 (toll-free from Lienz; toll tunnel from Salzburg/Bavaria). Complimentary car and coach parking as well as EV charging bays are located right at the center. The facility welcomes guests daily from May through October between 9:00 AM and 5:00 PM (winter schedules vary).

Tips

Speak with the ranger desk inside the atrium to book a guided wildlife safari into the dramatic Gschlößtal valley—frequently praised as the most breathtaking valley head in the Eastern Alps—to view wild bearded vultures and chamois through high-powered spotting scopes. Admission is free with the regional "Osttirol Card".
